title: Jobb Lenne, Ha... – Wishes About a Situation

sections.title: Flipping the order
sections.content: You already said Az jó lenne about a hypothetical outcome (Unit 28's neked kellene lesson). Put lenne first and add ha, and you get a whole pattern for wishing a situation were different: Jobb lenne, ha... ("It would be better if...") states the wish first, then the imagined change — and the ha-clause still takes the conditional, exactly like Ha lenne időm did.

sections.title: Wishing something were different
rows: It would be better if we left earlier.
It would be good if you rested more.
It would be worse if it rained.

items.english: It would be better if we left earlier.

items.spanish: Az lenne a megoldás, ha kevesebbet dolgoznék.
items.english: The solution would be for me to work less.

items.spanish: Jó lenne, ha nem esne, de rossz az időjárás.
items.english: It would be good if it weren't raining, but the weather is bad.

sections.content: Jobb lenne, ha... sounds like a wish about a situation, softer and less pointed than neked kellene from earlier this unit, which names exactly who should act.
